title: Remove logic re-derived per adapter and per call site
summary: Findings surfaced during P104 that had no owner: shared logic written once per adapter, a URL-rewrite technique re-derived three times, and a guard blind spot documented but untracked.
description:
Everything here was found while completing P104(F005) and left unowned. P104 fixed the instances that its own tasks named; these are the ones it revealed and did not cover. All were verified against the code on 2026-09-23, not carried over as claims.

The unifying fault is the one AGENTS.md rule 4 exists to prevent: a decision made in a shared place and then re-derived at each consumer. P104 hit four separate defects caused by exactly this, and the sweep below shows how much of it is left.

**1. Shared helpers written privately in both adapters.**

Ten functions are defined independently in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` and `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts`: `acceptedDecisionMutationFailure`, `applyTaskLifecycleDates`, `boundedPage`, `derivedStatusReadOnlyResult`, `handoffContractFailure`, `legacyContextMigrationSummary`, `mutationNoFieldsFailure`, `nowISO`, `resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget`, `resolveFeatureRefStrict`.

Three more are adapter-local copies of something plan-core already exports: `featureNumberOfPhase` (plan-mcp shadows `plan-core/naming.ts:120`, which pi-adapter imports correctly), `createRequirementId` (pi-adapter shadows `naming.ts`), `statusIcon` (pi-adapter shadows `render-utils.ts`).

The three shadowing cases are unambiguous: delete the copy, import the export. The ten are not uniformly movable, and the task that does this must not treat them as one blob — `handoffContractFailure` and `mutationNoFieldsFailure` return adapter-specific result shapes, so what belongs in the core is the decision and the message, with each adapter rendering its own envelope. That split is exactly what P104's successful tasks did (see `mutation-reply.ts`, `guard-decision.ts`, `task-completion-gate.ts`): the core decides and returns a text/structured pair, the adapter wraps it.

The sweep that produced this list should be recorded so it can be re-run rather than re-invented: parse `^(export )?(async )?function (\w+)` from both adapter entry points and from `packages/plan-core/src/*.ts`, then intersect. It takes seconds and catches the next one.

**2. Writing the URL without a router navigation, re-derived three times.**

`packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx:27` (`clearLocateParam`), `packages/plan-web-ui/src/routes/feature-detail/route.tsx:83`, and `packages/plan-web-ui/src/routes/phase-detail/route.tsx:75` each hand-write the same `window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", ...)` call, each with its own comment explaining the same reason: avoid a router navigation so React Router's `<ScrollRestoration />` does not reset the page scroll.

All three are correct today. The two route ones do not have the defect P104(F005)/T418 fixed in the work tree, because they only write the URL and never read the param back — the bug needed both halves. But the technique carries a non-obvious hazard that T418 documented the hard way: `replaceState` bypasses the router, so `useSearchParams` never observes the change, and any code that later reads that param sees a stale value for the life of the mount. A fourth site written by someone who has not read T418's comment is where that returns.

One helper, with the hazard stated once, removes the class. Whether it should also expose a read-side companion is a judgement for the task.

**3. The no-task guard cannot see a write made through an interpreter.**

P104(F005)/T427 made the guard detect write-shaped Bash — redirection, `tee`, in-place `sed`/`perl`, file-creating `cp`/`mv`, `rm`, tree-rewriting `git` — and deliberately documented what it cannot see rather than implying coverage: a command like `python3 - <<PY` or `node -e` that opens a file and writes to it is opaque from the command line.

This is not hypothetical. It is the exact pattern used to edit source files throughout the session that built P104, and it is what the harness instructs agents to use in bypass-permissions mode. So the most common editing path in that mode is the one the guard cannot see.

Whether this is worth closing is a real question and the task should answer it before writing code. Detecting interpreter writes reliably means either parsing the script body — brittle and endless — or moving the check elsewhere, such as a PostToolUse hook that notices the working tree changed while no task was in progress. A PostToolUse check cannot prevent the edit, but it can surface it, which may be the better fit for something whose purpose is visibility rather than prevention. Deciding not to close it, with the reason written down, is an acceptable outcome.

**Not in scope, recorded so it is not lost:** the branch `feature/handoff-retry-cost` carries 27 commits, has never been pushed, and has no PR. Antonio declined a PR twice during earlier phases and the reason was never recorded. That is a decision for him, not a task.

**Behaviors to preserve across all of this:** the core stays harness-agnostic (AGENTS.md rule 4) — moving adapter-specific result envelopes into it would be the same mistake in the opposite direction. The payload bounds established by P103 and P104 must not regress; `packages/plan-core/test/handoff-reply.test.mjs` pins them. Per AGENTS.md rule 17, focused suites during implementation and `pnpm verify:final` once at phase close.

tasks.title: Delete the adapter-local copies of shared logic
tasks.description:
Thirteen functions are written per adapter instead of once. Verified on 2026-09-23 by parsing function declarations out of both adapter entry points and every `packages/plan-core/src/*.ts`, then intersecting.

**Three are unambiguous — an adapter-local copy of something plan-core already exports.** Delete the copy, import the export:
- `featureNumberOfPhase` — `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:289` shadows `packages/plan-core/src/naming.ts:120`. pi-adapter already imports the core one, so the two adapters disagree about where this lives.
- `createRequirementId` — pi-adapter shadows `naming.ts`.
- `statusIcon` — pi-adapter shadows `render-utils.ts`.

**Ten are defined privately in BOTH adapters:** `acceptedDecisionMutationFailure`, `applyTaskLifecycleDates`, `boundedPage`, `derivedStatusReadOnlyResult`, `handoffContractFailure`, `legacyContextMigrationSummary`, `mutationNoFieldsFailure`, `resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget`, `resolveFeatureRefStrict`, `nowISO`.

Do not treat those ten as one blob. They fall into three kinds and the fix differs:

- *Pure logic with no adapter shape* — `nowISO`, `boundedPage`, `applyTaskLifecycleDates`, `resolveFeatureRefStrict`, `resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget`. These move to plan-core whole and both adapters import them.
- *A decision plus an adapter-specific envelope* — `handoffContractFailure`, `mutationNoFieldsFailure`, `acceptedDecisionMutationFailure`, `derivedStatusReadOnlyResult`. MCP returns `{ isError, content, structuredContent }`; Pi returns `{ content, details }`. Moving the envelope into the core would be rule 4 broken in the opposite direction. Move the decision and the message; let each adapter wrap its own result. This is the split every successful P104 task used — see `mutation-reply.ts`, `guard-decision.ts`, `task-completion-gate.ts`, each returning a text/structured pair the adapter renders.
- *Rendering* — `legacyContextMigrationSummary`. Decide deliberately which half is shared.

Before moving any of them, diff the two copies. Two implementations of the same name that have silently drifted is the more serious finding, and it is what this task most needs to surface: P104(F005)/T424 found exactly that shape in feature delete, where two of four copies had a data-integrity bug the other two did not. Report any divergence explicitly rather than picking one and moving on.

Steps:
1. Diff each pair. Record every divergence found, with which behaviour is correct and why.
2. Delete the three shadowing copies; import the core export.
3. Move the pure-logic five to plan-core; both adapters import.
4. For the four failure builders, move the decision and message; leave each envelope in its adapter.
5. Decide `legacyContextMigrationSummary` deliberately and say why.
6. Record the sweep as a check that can be re-run — a script or a test asserting no function name is defined in both adapter entry points — so the next copy is caught rather than accumulated.

Behaviors to preserve: every typed error code and result field exactly as it is; mutation-integrity checking across this project reads `updated`, `updatedFields` and `errorCode`. `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters` are enforced. Focused suites during work: plan-core, plan-mcp, pi-adapter, plan-server and agent-plan — all five, because a test in agent-plan went unnoticed for four commits during P104 when it was left out of that list.

Edge cases: a helper whose two copies differ only in a message string, where the wording is deliberately adapter-specific; a helper only one adapter actually calls, which may simply be dead in the other.

---
**Completion summary:**
Diffed all ten pairs before moving anything, then centralized per the three-kind split.

DIVERGENCES FOUND:
- statusIcon: REAL drift, now fixed. pi-adapter's local copy used deferred:"⏳" waiting:"⏱️"; plan-core's render-utils.ts (already used everywhere else — renderer.ts, export-service.ts, PLAN.md generation) uses deferred:"⏸️" waiting:"⏳". Pi's handoff markdown task list was showing different icons for these two statuses than PLAN.md shows for the same task in the same session. Deleted pi's copy, now imports core's (the version already canonical everywhere else) — this is the correct fix, not an arbitrary pick.
- A third, undeclared copy: packages/plan-server/src/serve.ts independently defines its own nowISO, applyTaskLifecycleDates (returns Task, not void — harmless extra return, callers ignore it), and resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget. The server's resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget is functionally WEAKER than the shared one: its feature lookup has no ambiguity detection or partial-name match, and its task lookup only matches task.id or a bare `T\d+` — no findTaskByRef, so composite refs (P00x/T00x), shortIds, and title fallback that MCP/Pi accept all fail over HTTP for the same operation. Left untouched — out of this task's literal scope (adapter entry points only, per the task description and phase's own sweep), and fixing it changes the HTTP API's accepted ref grammar, which needs its own decision and test coverage. Flagging as a follow-up.
- Everything else (boundedPage, resolveFeatureRefStrict, applyTaskLifecycleDates, resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget between the two adapters, legacyContextMigrationSummary, and the decision/message halves of handoffContractFailure/mutationNoFieldsFailure/acceptedDecisionMutationFailure/derivedStatusReadOnlyResult) was byte-identical or behaviorally equivalent between plan-mcp and pi-adapter. derivedStatusReadOnlyResult's retryAction line differs deliberately (tool name: planner-feature-update vs feature_update) — kept as adapter-supplied input, matching the task's own "edge case" callout.
- Also noticed (not fixed, different name so unaffected by the new check): pi-adapter has its own `pad()` that duplicates naming.ts's `formatThreeDigitNumber`.

WHAT MOVED:
- Shadowing copies deleted, now import the core export: featureNumberOfPhase (plan-mcp), createRequirementId + statusIcon (pi-adapter).
- Pure logic moved whole to plan-core, both adapters import: nowISO (exported from plan-store.ts, where it already lived privately), boundedPage (new packages/plan-core/src/pagination.ts), applyTaskLifecycleDates (new packages/plan-core/src/task-lifecycle.ts), resolveFeatureRefStrict (added to refs.ts), resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget + its two types (added to accepted-decision-guard.ts).
- legacyContextMigrationSummary: identical string-builder in both, no adapter shape at all — moved whole to project-context-migration.ts (rendering decision: nothing to split, it's already just data->text).
- Four failure builders split per the mutation-reply.ts pattern (text/structured pair from core, adapter renders its own envelope): handoffContractFailureReply (handoff-reply.ts), derivedStatusReadOnlyReply (mutation-reply.ts, retryAction is caller-supplied), acceptedDecisionMutationFailureReply (accepted-decision-guard.ts, still rethrows non-ACCEPTED_DECISION_ errors). mutationNoFieldsFailure needed no new core function — noMutableFieldsReceived already was the shared decision+message; only the envelope was adapter-local.
- Each adapter kept a thin per-adapter wrapper for these four, renamed with an mcp/pi prefix (mcpHandoffContractFailure/piHandoffContractFailure, etc.) — following the existing mcpContextReadActions/piContextReadActions convention — so the wrapper still exists once per adapter without violating the new "no shared function name" check.

RE-RUNNABLE CHECK (item 6): added test/adapter-shared-logic.test.mjs (auto-picked up by scripts/test-all.mjs's integration scope, same as the existing planner-skill-inventory.test.mjs pattern — regex-parses top-level function declarations, no fixtures). Two assertions: (1) zero function names declared in both packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts and packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts, (2) neither adapter re-declares a function plan-core already exports. Both pass now; ran it standalone (`node --test test/adapter-shared-logic.test.mjs`) — 2/2 green.

VERIFICATION: pnpm -w check (full monorepo tsc -b) — clean. All five required suites match baseline exactly: plan-core 445/445, plan-mcp 92/92 (node --test packages/plan-mcp/test/**/*.test.mjs), pi-adapter 93/93, plan-server 57/57 (untouched, confirms no fallout), agent-plan 14/14. noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters enforced by tsc -b and passed. Did not touch packages/plan-core/planner-skill.md, so plugins:sync/plugins:check were not needed.

Files changed: packages/plan-core/src/{index.ts,plan-store.ts,refs.ts,accepted-decision-guard.ts,mutation-reply.ts,handoff-reply.ts,project-context-migration.ts,pagination.ts(new),task-lifecycle.ts(new)}, packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts, packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts, test/adapter-shared-logic.test.mjs (new). Left uncommitted per instructions.

tasks.title: Write the URL without a router navigation in one place
tasks.description:
Three components hand-write the same `window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", ...)` call, each with its own comment giving the same reason.

- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/dashboard/work-tree.tsx:27` — `clearLocateParam`, stripping `?locate=` after scrolling the located row into view.
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/routes/feature-detail/route.tsx:83` — syncing filter state into the URL for deep-linking.
- `packages/plan-web-ui/src/routes/phase-detail/route.tsx:75` — the same, for phases.

The shared reason: a router navigation would make React Router's `<ScrollRestoration />` reset the page scroll, undoing a deliberate scroll or yanking the page while the user is filtering.

All three are correct today. The two route sites do not have the defect P104(F005)/T418 fixed in the work tree, because they only write the URL and never read the param back — that bug needed both halves.

The hazard is what makes this worth centralizing rather than leaving as three tidy copies: `replaceState` bypasses the router, so `useSearchParams()` never observes the change. Any code that later reads that param keeps seeing the old value for the life of the mount. In the work tree that turned into a user-visible bug — the locate effect kept firing and wiped the search box on every keystroke — and it took tracing the whole effect to find. The comment explaining it lives in `work-tree.tsx` and nowhere else. A fourth call site, written by someone who has not read that comment, is where this returns.

Desired state: one helper, with the hazard stated once where anyone using it will read it, and all three call sites using it.

Steps:
- Put the helper somewhere a route and a component both reach naturally — `packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/` is where the other shared browser utilities live.
- State both halves in its doc comment: why it avoids a router navigation, and that the router will not see the change, so a param written or cleared this way must not be read back through `useSearchParams` and trusted.
- Convert all three sites.
- Judgement call the task must make and record: whether to also expose a read-side companion that reads the param from `window.location` rather than the router, so the stale-read hazard has a safe answer rather than only a warning. Decide it deliberately; either answer is fine with a reason.

Behaviors to preserve: the work tree's scroll-and-pulse behaviour and its `handledLocateRef` guard from T418; both detail routes' deep-link filter syncing; no router navigation from any of the three.

Verification: focused Web UI suite (`pnpm test` in `packages/plan-web-ui`, 105 tests at last count including T418's four locate regressions) and `pnpm check`. Project guidelines require a unit test for a component touched; the existing `work-tree-locate.test.tsx` already covers the work-tree behaviour and must keep passing unchanged.

---
**Completion summary:**
Added packages/plan-web-ui/src/lib/browser-url.ts exporting replaceUrlSearchParams(mutate), which reads window.location, applies the mutator to a URLSearchParams, and only calls history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", url) when the resulting path/search/hash actually differs from before (a strict generalization of work-tree's old "only touch history if there's something to clear" early-return, done in the helper rather than at each call site). Its doc comment states both halves of the hazard: why replaceState avoids a router navigation (ScrollRestoration would reset scroll), and that useSearchParams() never observes the change, so a param written/cleared this way must never be read back through it.

Converted all three call sites to use it, no behavior change:
- work-tree.tsx:23 clearLocateParam() now calls replaceUrlSearchParams(params => params.delete("locate")); local comment points to the helper's doc and to handledLocateRef as the reason that hazard matters here.
- routes/feature-detail/route.tsx:76 and routes/phase-detail/route.tsx:70 — the five-param filter-sync effect now passes its sync() closure into replaceUrlSearchParams instead of building its own URL/replaceState call.

Judgement call (checklist C3): did not add a read-side companion (e.g. readUrlParam from window.location). None of the three call sites read a param back today — the task description itself notes the two route sites "only write the URL and never read the param back." Per the task's own instruction not to add a "just in case" export, I left this as a documented warning only: the helper's doc comment states the hazard and tells a future caller that needs to read a param written this way to read window.location.search directly rather than useSearchParams, but exports no unused function for it.

Verification: `pnpm check` (tsc --noEmit) clean. `pnpm test`: node suite 19/19 pass, vitest 105/105 pass across 15 files (matches stated baseline), including all 4 tests in test/work-tree-locate.test.tsx (T418 regressions) passing unchanged. Did not run pnpm verify:final per instructions (reserved for phase close). Nothing left broken or skipped.

tasks.title: Decide what to do about a write the guard cannot see
tasks.description:
P104(F005)/T427 made the no-task guard detect write-shaped Bash — output redirection, `tee`, in-place `sed`/`perl`, file-creating `cp`/`mv`, `rm`, tree-rewriting `git` — and deliberately documented what it cannot see instead of implying coverage. `packages/plan-core/src/guard-decision.ts` says so in the comment on `extractBashWriteTargets`.

The gap: a command that writes through an interpreter is opaque from the command line. `python3 - <<PY` followed by `open(path, "w").write(...)`, or `node -e`, or a script invoked by name, all edit files while the command string shows nothing write-shaped. Verified on 2026-09-23: a `python3` heredoc writing to `packages/plan-core/src/` is allowed silently, while the same write via `cat >` or `sed -i` correctly asks.

This is not a hypothetical corner. It is the exact pattern used to edit source files throughout the session that built P104, and the harness instructs agents to edit that way in bypass-permissions mode. So in that mode the most common editing path is the one the guard cannot see.

**Answer the question before writing code.** This task may correctly end with a recorded decision not to close the gap, and that is a real outcome, not a failure. The options are not equal:

- *Parse the script body.* Brittle and unbounded — a path can be computed, read from argv, or built at runtime. It would produce false confidence, which is worse than a documented limit, because the comment currently tells the truth.
- *Move the check after the fact.* A `PostToolUse` hook can notice that tracked files changed while no task was in progress. It cannot prevent the edit, but the guard's purpose is visibility, not prevention — `permissionDecision: "ask"` already assumes the user may say yes. Something that says "these files changed and no task was in progress" fits that purpose and is not defeated by how the write was made.
- *Leave it.* The limit is documented, the common cases are covered, and an agent editing through an interpreter in a bypass session is usually doing so because the harness told it to. Record the reasoning and close the task.

If the PostToolUse route is chosen: it must not fire on `.planner/` changes (P104(F005)/T427's firmest requirement — writing a handoff or recording task state is never blocked and should never be nagged about either), must not run on every tool call if that is expensive, and must not duplicate the write-detection already in `guard-decision.ts`. `plugins/claude-code/hooks/hooks.json` is where hooks are registered; `pnpm plugins:sync` and `pnpm plugins:check` after any change to a `.in` file.

Whatever is decided, update the comment in `guard-decision.ts` so it points at the decision rather than leaving a future reader to rediscover the question.

Verification: `packages/plan-core/test/guard-decision.test.mjs` (16 tests) and `packages/agent-plan/test/guard-pre-tool-use.test.mjs` (7 tests) are the existing coverage. If behaviour changes, prove the new test is live by reverting the change and confirming it fails. All five focused suites must stay green: plan-core, plan-mcp, pi-adapter, plan-server, agent-plan.

checklist.title: Decide between parsing, a PostToolUse check, and leaving it documented; record the reasoning
If a check is added: never fire on .planner/, reuse guard-decision.ts's detection
Update the comment in guard-decision.ts to point at the decision
All five focused suites green

tasks.title: Make a reference resolve the same way over HTTP as it does in the adapters
tasks.description:
`packages/plan-server/src/serve.ts` carries a third, independent copy of logic P105(F005)/T429 just consolidated for the two adapters — and its version is weaker, so the same reference that works from an agent fails from the Web UI.

Found during T429 and verified on 2026-09-24. T429's sweep was scoped to the two adapter entry points, so the server was out of its scope; the divergence is real and belongs in this phase.

**The behavioural gap.** `resolveAcceptedDecisionTarget` at `serve.ts:71` resolves a task at `:87` by raw UUID, or by a bare `T\d+` pattern, and nothing else:

    const found = phases.flatMap(...).find(({ task }) => task.id === targetRef)
      ?? (() => { const m = targetRef.match(/^T(\d+)$/i); ... })

Both adapters use `findTaskByRef` from plan-core, which additionally accepts the composite form (`P104(F005)/T428`), the 5-character shortId, and an exact title. So attaching an accepted decision to a task succeeds with `P104(F005)/T428` from MCP or Pi and fails with the same string over HTTP. Project decision D10 makes composite refs the canonical way to name an entity, which is precisely the form the HTTP path rejects.

Feature resolution at `:78` has a second, quieter problem: it takes the first match with no ambiguity detection, where `resolveFeatureRefStrict` (now in `packages/plan-core/src/refs.ts` after T429) reports an ambiguous reference instead of silently picking one. A caller naming two features by an overlapping title gets a silent wrong answer over HTTP and an error everywhere else.

**Also duplicated in the same file:** `nowISO` at `:21` and `applyTaskLifecycleDates` at `:152`. Both now live in plan-core (`plan-store.ts` and the new `task-lifecycle.ts`). `applyTaskLifecycleDates` is the one that matters — it sets `startedAt` / `completedAt` on a status change, so a drift between the two copies would mean a task completed over HTTP carries different lifecycle dates than the same task completed by an agent. Diff them before replacing, and report any divergence found: that comparison is the valuable part, exactly as it was in T429, where `statusIcon` turned out to have been showing ⏳ for `deferred` in one surface while core used ⏳ for `waiting`.

**Steps:**
1. Diff the server's three copies against the plan-core versions. Record any divergence and which behaviour is correct.
2. Replace them with the core functions: `findTaskByRef` and `resolveFeatureRefStrict` for resolution, `nowISO` and `applyTaskLifecycleDates` for the rest.
3. Extend T429's duplication check (`test/adapter-shared-logic.test.mjs`) to cover `plan-server/src/serve.ts` as a third entry point, so this cannot regrow. That check is proven live — re-introducing a duplicate makes it fail.
4. Verify the HTTP path now accepts a composite ref, a shortId and a title for a task, and reports ambiguity for a feature.

**Behaviors to preserve:** the server is a supervisor surface and some of its permissiveness is deliberate — the legacy `decisions` array stays writable over HTTP and refused on agent tools, by an accepted decision from P103(F005)/T405. Do not tighten that. This task is about a reference resolving consistently, not about making the Web UI obey agent-only gates. Every existing response shape and WebSocket broadcast stays as it is; `packages/plan-server/test/` is 57 tests and must stay green.

**Edge case worth deciding:** whether the HTTP path should accept a bare `T\d+` at all once composite refs work. It is ambiguous across phases in a project with global numbering, and dropping it would be a breaking change for any existing Web UI caller. Decide deliberately and say why.

checklist.title: Diff the server's three copies against plan-core; record any divergence
Replace resolution with findTaskByRef and resolveFeatureRefStrict
Replace nowISO and applyTaskLifecycleDates with the core versions
Extend the duplication check to cover serve.ts as a third entry point
Verify composite ref, shortId and title resolve over HTTP; ambiguity is reported
Decide whether bare T\d+ stays, and say why
